variants.headline: Party leader faces a challenge
variants.sub: A challenge to the leadership of {party} has opened.
variants.body:
The leader of {party} is being challenged. The challenge places authority within the organisation in question, without deciding who should exercise it. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the opening of a contest from an outcome that has not been established by this report.

There is a challenge to a party leader. Give {target} a fair hearing; outrage alone should not be allowed to write the whole verdict.

variants.headline: Leadership becomes a contested question
variants.sub: Leadership of the party {party} is under challenge.
variants.body:
A challenge to the leadership of {party} has opened. That is the political development, rather than proof of an eventual removal or victory. An examination of {target} should begin with the challenge itself and leave the candidates' unreported programmes outside the factual account.

There is a challenge to a party leader. Give {target} a fair hearing; outrage alone should not be allowed to write the whole verdict.

variants.headline: A challenge inside the party
variants.sub: The leader of {party} is being challenged.
variants.body:
Leadership of the party {party} is under challenge. A party leader now faces a challenge in {colony}. For {target}, the relevant issue is the exercise and scrutiny of political authority, not an imagined story about who has already secured the organisation's support.

There is a challenge to a party leader. Give {target} a fair hearing; outrage alone should not be allowed to write the whole verdict.
